cholestasis.description: Bile retained in liver tissue because bile formation or drainage is impaired.
cholestasis.histology: Look for yellow-green to brown bile pigment in hepatocytes and plugs within the tiny canaliculi between them.
cholestasis.context: This is a pattern of bile retention; it does not identify the cause of obstruction or liver injury.

extramedullary_hematopoiesis.description: Blood-cell production outside the bone marrow, here within the liver.
extramedullary_hematopoiesis.histology: Look for groups of nucleated red-cell precursors, myeloid precursors and occasional large megakaryocytes between hepatocytes or in sinusoids.
extramedullary_hematopoiesis.context: Interpret with age: hepatic blood-cell production can persist in fetal and early neonatal life.

hemozoin_pigment.description: Pigment produced as malaria parasites digest haemoglobin.
hemozoin_pigment.histology: Look for coarse brown to black granules within enlarged Kupffer cells along the liver sinusoids.
hemozoin_pigment.context: Pigment supports malaria exposure, but does not by itself establish active infection; correlate with parasite testing.

hepatic_inflammation_portal.description: Inflammatory cells concentrated in the liver's portal tracts.
hepatic_inflammation_portal.histology: Find a portal vein branch, artery and bile duct, then look for an expanded cuff or cluster of inflammatory cells around these structures.
hepatic_inflammation_portal.context: The label describes the location of inflammation; it does not establish a specific infection or hepatitis subtype.

hepatic_inflammation_sinusoidal.description: Inflammatory cells within the small vascular channels between liver-cell plates.
hepatic_inflammation_sinusoidal.histology: Look for increased nucleated inflammatory cells along sinusoids between hepatocytes, rather than a predominantly portal-tract infiltrate.
hepatic_inflammation_sinusoidal.context: This is a distribution pattern, not a specific cause. Distinguish inflammatory cells from blood-cell precursors in hematopoiesis.

liver_congestion.description: Excess blood within the liver's vascular channels.
liver_congestion.histology: Look for dilated sinusoids packed with red cells, often most prominent around central veins.
liver_congestion.context: The appearance describes congestion; clinical context is needed to identify its cause.

steatosis.histology: Look for clear, round vacuoles in hepatocyte cytoplasm. Large droplets may displace the nucleus toward the cell edge.
steatosis.context: The label describes fat, not its cause or the presence of steatohepatitis.

aspiration_meconium.description: Meconium-containing material inhaled into the fetal or newborn lung.
aspiration_meconium.histology: Look for rounded clumps of meconium within airspaces, often accompanied by flat fetal squamous cells.
aspiration_meconium.context: Squamous cells alone are not evidence that meconium is present.

aspiration_squames.description: Fetal skin cells from amniotic fluid present in lung airspaces.
aspiration_squames.histology: Look for thin, flat, pink squamous flakes within bronchioles or alveolar spaces; they may occur beside meconium.
aspiration_squames.context: This records aspirated material; squames alone do not establish clinically significant aspiration injury.

bronchopneumonia.description: Patchy acute inflammation involving small airways and nearby alveoli, commonly associated with infection.
bronchopneumonia.histology: Look for clusters of neutrophils filling bronchioles and surrounding alveoli, creating patchy areas of consolidation.
bronchopneumonia.context: The pattern does not identify a particular organism; microbiology or additional stains may be needed.

fibrin.description: Clotting protein deposited in lung airspaces during leakage or injury.
fibrin.histology: Look for pink fibrillary, stringy or mesh-like material within alveoli, sometimes mixed with inflammatory cells.
fibrin.context: Fibrin can occur in several injury patterns. Distinguish free airspace strands from a membrane coating an alveolar wall.

hyaline_membranes.description: Protein-rich material and cellular debris coating injured alveolar surfaces.
hyaline_membranes.histology: Look for smooth, dense pink bands lining alveolar walls, rather than loose material in the centre of an airspace.
hyaline_membranes.context: Seen in diffuse alveolar damage and neonatal respiratory distress; the finding alone does not identify the cause.

increased_alveolar_macrophages.description: More scavenger immune cells than usual within the lung airspaces.
increased_alveolar_macrophages.histology: Look for numerous large cells with abundant pale or foamy cytoplasm and round to oval nuclei inside alveoli; some contain brown pigment.
increased_alveolar_macrophages.context: Macrophages normally occur in small numbers. An increase is a response pattern and does not specify one disease.

lung_congestion.description: Excess blood within the vessels of the lung.
lung_congestion.histology: Look for dilated capillaries packed with red cells within the alveolar walls; airspace oedema may accompany them.
lung_congestion.context: In congestion, red cells are mainly inside capillaries. Free red cells filling airspaces suggest accompanying haemorrhage.

lung_hemorrhage.description: Blood escaping from vessels into lung tissue or airspaces.
lung_hemorrhage.histology: Look for free red blood cells filling alveoli outside the septal capillaries. Older bleeding may leave macrophages containing brown haemosiderin.
lung_hemorrhage.context: Assess the distribution and tissue quality; the presence of blood alone does not identify why bleeding occurred.

pneumonitis.description: A broad label for lung inflammation, often involving the alveolar walls.
pneumonitis.histology: Look for inflammatory cells expanding alveolar septa, sometimes with reactive lining cells. Compare with neutrophils predominantly filling airspaces in bronchopneumonia.
pneumonitis.context: The label is nonspecific: inflammation alone does not distinguish infectious from noninfectious causes.

preterm_lung.description: Immature lung architecture reflecting an earlier stage of development.
preterm_lung.histology: Look for relatively simple distal airspaces with broad, cellular septa and fewer secondary septal crests than in more mature lung.
preterm_lung.context: Interpret with gestational age. Immaturity and hyaline membranes are separate findings and may coexist.
